title: Navigation innovation laboratory: active localization, asynchronous fix scheduling and selective model adaptation
summary: Three stdlib synthetic POCs with conventional baselines, ablations, held-out seeds, stress cases and paired intervals. Tests possible contributions rather than claiming novelty; exposes map-shift failures, harmful slowdown and limits of model adaptation. A separate causal replay evaluates cached VPAIR observations under artificial frame delays and an uncalibrated covariance proxy; no consistent scheduling advantage.
verified: Ran 2026-11-09 on Python 3.9.6/macOS arm64: 8000 synthetic evaluation episodes, 100 seeds per scenario, disjoint from 16 tuning seeds; 19 stdlib unit tests. Source hashes, tuning grids and all per-seed metrics committed. No images, aircraft dynamics, SITL, hardware or field validation; offline network-denial test not performed. Also ran 48 cached VPAIR replay cases, with hashes of three sibling input files; real-flight-derived inputs but artificial timing and a simplified filter.
shows: Compare three proposed mechanisms with stronger conventional baselines and retain negative findings
input: synthetic; optional recorded-flight-derived replay with artificial timing
runtime: about 11 seconds on the recorded host
key_result: [Evidence](README.md#what-survived-the-first-experiment): H1 equals information gain; H2 opportunity baseline competitive; H3 helps after observable changes but loses to initial calibration nominally

readiness.limitation: Primary benchmark uses synthetic descriptor/scalar models; optional replay is one previously studied flight with artificial frame delays, not field validation.
